title: Snowflake motif — joined
subtitle: Six basic snowflakes linked at arm tips into a circular wreath, 28 cm across
excerpt: The joined snowflake links six individual basic snowflakes at adjacent arm tips with a short chain join, forming a circular wreath with a central opening. The finished piece is 28 cm across in 4-ply cotton and is used as a window hanging, wreath base, or table centrepiece. Each snowflake is worked separately then linked on the final arm.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 5 (1890), joined snowflake and lace medallion chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), joined crochet star chapter.

chartDefinition.title: Snowflake motif — joined
chartDefinition.caption: Six basic snowflakes (see crochet-snowflake-basic) joined at arm tips with ch-3 joins. The chart shows one snowflake unit with the join positions marked. Snowflakes 2 through 6 replace two arm-tip dc stitches with join slip stitches into adjacent arms.

glossaryTerms.definition: A technique where the joining stitch is worked as part of the final motif's border, eliminating the need for a separate seaming step.

content.text: The joined snowflake wreath uses the basic snowflake construction (see crochet-snowflake-basic) for all six units, with a
join-as-you-go

method on the final two arms of each snowflake 2 through 6. Snowflake 1 is worked complete and free. Snowflake 2 is worked with two adjacent arms joined to snowflake 1 by substituting the dc arm tip with a ch-3 join into the neighbour arm. Snowflakes 3 through 6 continue in the same way around the ring.

The join is a ch-3 loop from the working arm tip, slip stitched into the tip of the adjacent arm on the already-completed snowflake, then ch-3 back and continued. The join keeps the arm tips at the same distance apart as free arm tips are from their rings, preserving the visual rhythm.

attrs.title: Materials for one wreath
attrs.body: About 20 g of white 4-ply cotton for all six snowflakes. A 2.5 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Fabric starch is recommended for a window hanging. Blocking mat and T-pins.

content.text: Gauge
Each individual snowflake measures 8 cm across. The joined wreath measures 28 cm across in 4-ply cotton with a 2.5 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
Pattern
Snowflake 1 — work complete
Work crochet-snowflake-basic exactly as written — all 6 arms complete and free. Fasten off and weave in ends.
Snowflakes 2 through 5 — joined on two arms

Work the centre ring and the first four arms exactly as for crochet-snowflake-basic. For the fifth arm (the arm that will meet the previous snowflake): Ch 8. Instead of dc into the 2nd ch, work ch 3, sl st into the corresponding arm tip of the previous snowflake, ch 3, sl st back to the working chain, sl st along the chain to the ring. For the sixth arm, join similarly to the snowflake on the other adjacent side. Fasten off and weave in ends. (Each inner snowflake joins to the two neighbours on either side.)
Snowflake 6 — closing the wreath

Work the centre ring. Work the first two arms free. For arms 3 through 6, join to both adjacent snowflakes as described. On the last two arms, snowflake 6 also joins to snowflake 1 to close the circle. Check alignment before working the closing joins.

definition.title: Snowflake motif — joined
definition.caption: Six snowflake units in a ring. Free arm: ch-8, dc tip, ch-3, sl-st return. Joined arm: ch-8, ch-3 join into neighbour tip, ch-3, sl-st return.

content.text: Finishing
Weave in all ends. Dip in fabric starch solution, pin flat to a blocking mat at each outer arm tip, and dry fully. Attach a hanging loop to one outer arm tip with a length of thread.
Care
Handwash gently in cool water. Re-starch and re-pin flat to dry if the piece is used as a window hanging and has lost its rigidity.
What to try next

The intricate snowflake (crochet-snowflake-intricate) uses the same arm construction with branching picots. The star wreath (crochet-themed-star-wreath) uses a similar joined-motif approach with five-pointed star tiles.
